name: SpatialIngest
title: Spatial Ingest
description: Turn raw text into needs — or one product row — in the spatial dictionary.
whenToUse: Put raw text INTO the spatial map so it can be found later: notes, a transcript, a scraped page, a message thread, a parsed document pack. It reads the text, pulls out the distinct needs it describes — pain points, goals, intentions — embeds each one and stores it. Switched to Product, it instead stores ONE offering row for the whole text, for when the text in hand IS a complete offering's material; give it a source identity so the product and its needs stay linked. Switched to Component, it captures a FILLED component's completion output as that one product row — the page's document stored verbatim, its state kept for re-rendering. It only WRITES to that map — searching it is a different job — and it takes material that is already in hand rather than fetching from anywhere. Web pages become products by promoting them from the Content tree instead.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Upstream data. The text itself is named in config, usually templated from here.

outputs.name: universalIds
outputs.description: Ids of the stored entries, when the engine reports them

rawContent.title: Raw Content
rawContent.description: The text to read. Usually wired in from an upstream node.

category.title: Creates
category.description: What this text becomes. Needs: the distinct needs the text describes, one row each. Product: ONE offering row for the whole text — use only when the text is a source's complete material, and set a Source URL or Source ID so the product and its needs share one source identity. Component: ONE product row CAPTURED from a filled component's completion output — wire Raw Content to its markdown and the three component fields below to its state, document and URI; the document is stored VERBATIM as the row's body and the state as its render payload.

componentState.title: Component State
componentState.description: The completed component's state — wire the completion output's `state` (the row's render payload, stored on metadata.state).

componentDocument.title: Component Document
componentDocument.description: The completed component's document — typed unoverse-markdown sections, stored VERBATIM as the row's bodyCopy.

componentUri.title: Component URI
componentUri.description: The component's URI from the completion output — stored as metadata.app so the row renders as this component.

sourceUrl.title: Source URL
sourceUrl.description: Where the text came from, kept for provenance. Optional.

sourceId.title: Source ID
sourceId.description: Stable id of the source this text came from (e.g. the S3 file's universalId). Blank = derived from the Source URL.

metadata.title: Metadata (JSON)
metadata.description: Optional JSON object stamped onto every need from this text, e.g. {"documentTitle": "Q3 Deck", "client": "Acme"}. You choose the keys; future search can filter by them.

maxItems.title: Max Items
maxItems.description: Cap on how many entries to store from this text. Leave blank for no cap.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: ingest
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# INGEST, migrating one node at a time.
#
# Abyssale is the first. The other three are still TypeScript and each is blocked on something
# different, which is worth writing down because the package name suggests otherwise — "ingest REST
# nodes" was on the backlog as ready, and reading them proved it wrong:
#
#   PlaidTransactions  MIGRATED 2026-07-28 needing NO new capability, which is not what this note said a
#                      day earlier. All three of its supposed blockers dissolved once the vendor API was
#                      read rather than the old code.
#   GoogleSheet        MIGRATED as a REWRITE: it was a Sheets client AND a loop in one node, holding rows
#                      in actor state. It returns every row now and LoopStart/LoopEnd iterate.
#   DocumentParser     RETIRED and REPLACED by unstructured/ParseDocument. It parsed pdf/docx in process
#                      with `pdf-parse` and `mammoth`, which no manifest can express — and did not need
#                      to, once one HTTP call covered the same job and twenty more formats.
#   Document           RETIRED with no replacement: it existed to feed DocumentParser, and every metadata
#                      field it emitted came from its own input.
#   SpatialIngest      MIGRATED 2026-07-28 by DELETING the pipeline rather than describing it. It had
#                      reimplemented the content engine — 373 lines, 220 of them a drifted COPY of the
#                      engine's extraction prompts and schemas, with its own embedding call and its own
#                      write to the dictionary. The engine's MANUAL connector was written for this node
#                      and never used. Now it hands raw text over and the engine does the rest.

name: ingest
displayName: Ingest
description: Content ingestion, template rendering and data import
version: 2.1.0
category: ingest
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Render branded images and PDFs from Abyssale templates
  - Fetch realistic test bank transactions from Plaid Sandbox
  - Read rows from a public Google Sheet

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK, numeric form (the pattern rejects a bare "localhost"): SpatialIngest hands its
  # text to the platform's own content engine over `scope.engineUrl` (127.0.0.1:4101), same
  # declaration the spatial package carries for its searches.
  - 127.0.0.1
  - api.abyssale.com
  # Plaid picks its host from the credential's environment, so all three are declared. A sandbox key
  # cannot reach production and vice versa, so listing them is not a widening.
  - sheets.googleapis.com
  - sandbox.plaid.com
  - development.plaid.com
  - production.plaid.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"
  # apiKeyHeader for Abyssale (x-api-key), apiKeyQuery for Google Sheets (?key=). Plaid needs
  # neither: it authenticates in the request BODY, so it declares no scheme at all.
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  # Abyssale generation is asynchronous: POST to start, then ask the generation request until it is
  # finalized. Without `poll` the node would settle on the RECEIPT — a request id — and emit that as
  # the finished asset, with nothing reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.abyssaleCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: abyssaleCredential
displayName: Abyssale
description: Abyssale API credentials for high-quality template rendering

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Abyssale API key from the dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Abyssale API key
credentials.googleApiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# MOVED HERE, not copied, and moved NOW even though GoogleSheet is still TypeScript.
#
# Credential declaration is all-or-nothing per package: `registerCredentialType` is
# first-wins-and-SILENT, so a credentials/*.yaml alongside a live `api.registerCredential()` means
# whichever loads first takes the slot and the other vanishes — surfacing later as an auth failure
# with the right credential visibly selected. Migrating ONE node therefore moves EVERY credential the
# package declares.
#
# Nothing breaks for the code nodes: the type registry is shared, so GoogleSheet reads
# `googleApiCredential` exactly as before. Only the source of the declaration changed.

name: googleApiCredential
displayName: Google API
description: Google API credentials for accessing Google services

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Google API key with Sheets API enabled
    placeholder: Enter your Google API key
credentials.plaidCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Moved with the others — see googleApiCredential.yaml for why declaration is all-or-nothing.

name: plaidCredential
displayName: Plaid
description: Plaid API credentials for accessing banking data (Sandbox/Development/Production)

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Your Plaid client ID from the Plaid Dashboard
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid client ID
  - name: secret
    displayName: Secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Plaid secret key (use Sandbox secret for testing)
    placeholder: Enter your Plaid secret
  - name: environment
    displayName: Environment
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: "Plaid environment: sandbox, development, or production"
    placeholder: sandbox
    default: sandbox

files.api/events.yaml:
# `response` is the FINAL job status, not the receipt — that is what `poll` settles on.

- emit: success
  value: "return response.status === 'COMPLETED'"

- emit: count
  # `processedRows` is the engine's own count of rows taken all the way through extract, embed and save,
  # which is what "how many entries were stored" means. `totalItems` counts what was FETCHED, and for the
  # MANUAL connector that is always 1 — the single blob of text — so reading it would report 1 forever.
  value: "return ((response.progress || {}).processedRows) || 0"

- emit: universalIds
  # EMPTY, and honestly so. The code version minted these ids itself and could therefore list them; the
  # engine mints them now and its job status reports counts rather than ids. Emitting [] is the truthful
  # answer until the engine's status carries them — inventing ids here, or re-deriving them from the text,
  # would produce values that do not match the rows actually written.
  value: "return []"
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE CALL TO THE PLATFORM'S OWN CONTENT ENGINE, which already owns this pipeline.
#
# WHAT THIS NODE USED TO DO, and no longer does. The code version ran the whole thing itself: it called
# the platform's /execute to run OpenAIStructuredOutput, embedded the results against OpenAI directly,
# built the entries, and POSTed them to /dictionary/upload. 373 lines, 220 of them a COPY of the engine's
# extraction prompts and schemas, carrying a `TODO: move to shared package so there is one source of
# truth` — and the two copies had already drifted to different category sets.
#
# The engine's MANUAL connector was written FOR this node ("Used by the SpatialIngest workflow node to
# push raw text through the full content engine pipeline") and was never used. So this is not a redesign,
# it is finishing what was started: the node collects text and hands it over, and the schema, the prompts,
# the embedding credential and the database write stay in the one place that owns them.
#
# `connector: MANUAL` IS FIXED, not a dropdown. The other connectors fetch from somewhere — Cloudinary,
# Google Sheets, a scraper — and those are wired as their own nodes on the canvas. This node exists for
# text a workflow already has.
#
# THE HOST IS DERIVED, and it is the ENGINE. `scope.engineUrl` is :4101, where the content
# routes live (/content/ingest, /content/ingestion/:id) — NOT `scope.platformUrl` (:4106, the
# unoverse runtime: /service-call, /execute, /skills). Same split SpatialSearch documents in
# spatial/shared/search.yaml; picking the wrong listener is a 404 on every run (observed
# 2026-08-07). The code version read UNOVERSE_SERVICE_URL — a variable set nowhere in the repo
# — behind a hardcoded localhost fallback, so the fallback was the whole behaviour.

- name: ingest
  method: POST
  url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/content/ingest'"
  transport: json

  body:
    input:
      connector: MANUAL
      # The MANUAL connector's own config shape: { text, sourceUrl? }.
      config:
        text: "{{ config.rawContent }}"
        sourceUrl: "{{ config.sourceUrl }}"
        # The standard source identity, verbatim (migration 021). Blank renders empty and
        # resolveBody omits the key; the write chokepoint then derives one from sourceUrl.
        sourceId: "{{ config.sourceId }}"
        # Free-form caller metadata, stamped onto every extracted need (the caller owns the
        # vocabulary — future search filters by these keys). A JSON string in config, parsed
        # here: invalid JSON throws and fails the run loudly instead of storing garbage.
        # Single expression starting with `return` — that prefix is what marks a body value
        # as an expression rather than a template (resolveBody).
        # THE MODE GUARANTEES LIVE HERE, in the node's own body, where wiring cannot
        # lose them. Product mode stamps `promoted: true` LAST (over any caller key) —
        # the governance guarantee the category toggle's return was conditioned on
        # (SPATIAL_INGEST_NODE.md, 2026-08-18). Component mode (the completion
        # contract) additionally stamps the row's captured faces: `bodyCopy` = the
        # flat MARKDOWN verbatim (rawContent — a STRING, because every bodyCopy
        # reader renders it as markdown text; the typed document in there crashed
        # the Canvas content detail, seen live 2026-08-21), `sections` = the typed
        # sections VERBATIM — `sections` and not some private key, because that is
        # THE render key: every SDUI reader (ServiceRenderer, the editors) draws
        # `metadata.sections` through toDocument, so the captured page renders as
        # a designed document instead of falling back to flat markdown — `state` =
        # the render payload, `app` = the component URI. The uploader spreads
        # caller metadata LAST, so these override the LLM-generated body —
        # verified against prepareMetadata.
        # JSON.parse fails the run LOUDLY when a component field is unwired or empty —
        # a captured product with no state or document is a mis-wiring, never a row.
        metadata: "return config.category === 'component' ? Object.assign({}, config.metadata && String(config.metadata).trim() ? JSON.parse(config.metadata) : {}, { promoted: true, app: config.componentUri, state: JSON.parse(config.componentState), sections: JSON.parse(config.componentDocument), bodyCopy: String(config.rawContent || '') }) : config.category === 'product' ? Object.assign({}, config.metadata && String(config.metadata).trim() ? JSON.parse(config.metadata) : {}, { promoted: true }) : (config.metadata && String(config.metadata).trim() ? JSON.parse(config.metadata) : undefined)"
      # `need` → NEED (many rows, one per distinct need). `product` AND `component` →
      # SERVICE, the engine's 1:1 strict-grounded lane — the SAME extraction path
      # promote-page uses, one offering row for the whole text. The toggle returned
      # 2026-08-18 and grew component mode 2026-08-19 (owner rulings, decision record in
      # SPATIAL_INGEST_NODE.md); web pages still become products via promote-page — these
      # lanes are for material a workflow already holds whole.
      mainCategory: "return config.category === 'product' || config.category === 'component' ? 'SERVICE' : 'NEED'"
      # The engine keys everything by workflow, which is how a dictionary stays scoped to its universe.
      workflowId: "{{ scope.workflowId }}"
    maxItems: "return config.maxItems || undefined"

  timeoutMs: 60000

  # The job STARTS here and finishes below. A 200 carrying an error body must not read as success.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"

  # THE JOB, WAITED ON. `/content/ingest` returns a receipt — { jobId, status } — and settling on that
  # would emit "started" as though it meant "stored", so a downstream node would run against a dictionary
  # that has not been written yet.
  poll:
    url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/content/ingestion/' + response.jobId"
    # Done when it stops moving. The engine reports its stage as it goes (FETCHING, EXTRACTING,
    # EMBEDDING, SAVING), so the terminal states are named rather than the live ones.
    until: "return ['COMPLETED', 'FAILED', 'CANCELLED', 'INTERRUPTED'].includes(response.status)"
    # FAILED IS NOT FINISHED. INTERRUPTED is the engine's own word for "the server restarted mid-run",
    # which is a real outcome and must not read as success.
    failed: "return ['FAILED', 'CANCELLED', 'INTERRUPTED'].includes(response.status)"
    message: "return response.error || ('ingestion ' + response.status)"
    intervalMs: 2000
    # ~10 minutes. Extraction and embedding are per-item LLM calls, so a long document is genuinely slow.
    maxAttempts: 300
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

# NO CREDENTIAL, and that is the point of this node's rewrite. The code version held an
# `openAICredential` because it called OpenAI directly for embeddings. The engine owns that now, along
# with the extraction schema and the prompts, so the node carries no key at all.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [rawContent]
  properties:
    rawContent:
      type: string
      title: Raw Content
      description: The text to read. Usually wired in from an upstream node.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    # THE CATEGORY TOGGLE, back and SCOPED (owner ruling 2026-08-18, reversing the
    # 2026-08-07 removal — the decision record is SPATIAL_INGEST_NODE.md, amended first).
    # The 7 Aug objection was a raw-text product lane WITHOUT the promote lane's
    # guarantees; product mode here carries them: whole-source grounding (the SERVICE
    # extraction path, 1:1, strict grounding — the same path promote-page uses), the
    # standard source identity (set Source URL or Source ID so the product row and its
    # need rows share one source_id), and a metadata.promoted stamp (run.yaml adds it)
    # so the Content tree governs the row. Web PAGES still become products via
    # promote-page; this mode is for text a workflow already holds whole — e.g. a parsed
    # document pack whose offering row must join its needs on the map.
    category:
      type: string
      title: Creates
      description: >-
        What this text becomes. Needs: the distinct needs the text describes, one row
        each. Product: ONE offering row for the whole text — use only when the text is a
        source's complete material, and set a Source URL or Source ID so the product and
        its needs share one source identity. Component: ONE product row CAPTURED from a
        filled component's completion output — wire Raw Content to its markdown and the
        three component fields below to its state, document and URI; the document is
        stored VERBATIM as the row's body and the state as its render payload.
      enum: [need, product, component]
      enumNames: [Needs, Product (from text), Product (from component)]
      default: need
    # COMPONENT MODE (the completion contract, UNOVERSE_MCP_APP_PROTOCOL.md §The
    # completion contract): these three wire from the Component node's exit output,
    # which fires ONCE when the filler calls `complete`. The mode's guarantees live in
    # run.yaml's own body — bodyCopy verbatim, state + app + promoted stamped — so a
    # builder cannot mis-wire them away. All three are REQUIRED in component mode:
    # run.yaml JSON-parses state and document, so an unwired field fails the run loudly.
    componentState:
      type: string
      title: Component State
      description: The completed component's state — wire the completion output's `state` (the row's render payload, stored on metadata.state).
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { category: component }
    componentDocument:
      type: string
      title: Component Document
      description: The completed component's document — typed unoverse-markdown sections, stored VERBATIM as the row's bodyCopy.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { category: component }
    componentUri:
      type: string
      title: Component URI
      description: The component's URI from the completion output — stored as metadata.app so the row renders as this component.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:dependencies": { category: component }
    sourceUrl:
      type: string
      title: Source URL
      description: Where the text came from, kept for provenance. Optional.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    sourceId:
      type: string
      title: Source ID
      # THE standard source identity (migration 021): stored VERBATIM in the row's
      # source_id column, so future search can scope to one source. Wire in the id the
      # source node already mints — e.g. {{signal.s3filecontent1.file.universalId}} for
      # an S3 document. Left blank, the platform derives one from the Source URL.
      description: Stable id of the source this text came from (e.g. the S3 file's universalId). Blank = derived from the Source URL.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    metadata:
      type: string
      title: Metadata (JSON)
      # FREE-FORM BY DESIGN (platform owner's ruling, 2026-08-07): the caller decides the
      # vocabulary — documentTitle, client, quarter, whatever future search will filter by.
      # Stored verbatim on every need extracted from this text (the extractor merges the
      # source's metadata onto each entry). A template STRING holding JSON, not an object
      # field, because the config form has no JSON field type yet (backlog 2026-08-01);
      # run.yaml parses it and fails the run loudly on invalid JSON.
      description: 'Optional JSON object stamped onto every need from this text, e.g. {"documentTitle": "Q3 Deck", "client": "Acme"}. You choose the keys; future search can filter by them.'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    maxItems:
      type: number
      title: Max Items
      description: Cap on how many entries to store from this text. Leave blank for no cap.
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 500
"ui:order": [category, rawContent, componentState, componentDocument, componentUri, sourceUrl, sourceId, metadata, maxItems]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Upstream data. The text itself is named in config, usually templated from here.
    required: false

# THE NAMES ARE THE CODE VERSION'S, unchanged, because a saved workflow references an output by name.
#
# `universalIds` is the one that changed MEANING rather than name, and it is worth knowing: the code
# version minted those ids itself, so it could list them. The engine mints them now, and its job status
# reports counts rather than ids — so this emits [] until the engine returns them. See api/events.yaml.
outputs:
  - name: success
    type: boolean
    description: Whether the ingestion job completed
  - name: count
    type: number
    description: How many entries were stored
  - name: universalIds
    type: array
    description: Ids of the stored entries, when the engine reports them

credentials: []
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: SpatialIngest
kind: PromiseNode

name: Spatial Ingest
category: Documents
color: "#7C3AED"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

description: Turn raw text into needs — or one product row — in the spatial dictionary.

whenToUse: >-
  Put raw text INTO the spatial map so it can be found later: notes, a transcript, a scraped page, a
  message thread, a parsed document pack. It reads the text, pulls out the distinct needs it describes —
  pain points, goals, intentions — embeds each one and stores it. Switched to Product, it instead stores
  ONE offering row for the whole text, for when the text in hand IS a complete offering's material; give
  it a source identity so the product and its needs stay linked. Switched to Component, it captures a
  FILLED component's completion output as that one product row — the page's document stored verbatim,
  its state kept for re-rendering. It only WRITES to that map — searching it is a different job — and it
  takes material that is already in hand rather than fetching from anywhere. Web pages become products
  by promoting them from the Content tree instead.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). `required: false`, like almost every
# other node: the trigger already decided who was let in. This WAS `required: true`
# ("the write is attributed to the caller") — but the claim was never true: the ingest
# route carries no user and the dictionary row stores none; rows are scoped to the
# WORKFLOW. A floor that demands identity for an attribution never made is theater, and
# it also made the per-box "Require sign-in" toggle a silent no-op (owner ruling
# 2026-08-19). If per-user attribution is ever added to dictionary writes, the floor
# comes back WITH the attribution, not before it.
#
# No `role` yet: no deployment issues a spatial claim, so naming one would fail every run.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: it WRITES. A reused answer would report a store that never happened.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# THIS FIXTURE NEEDS THE PLATFORM RUNNING, which makes it the only one in the tree that does. Every other
# node reaches a vendor over the internet; this one calls the engine on 127.0.0.1:4106, so `unoverse node
# test SpatialIngest` fails with a connection error unless the service is up.
#
# It also WRITES: a successful run stores real entries in the dictionary for `workflowId`. The bench has
# no run behind it, so scope.workflowId is empty and the engine scopes the rows to "" — which is worth
# knowing before running it against a database you care about.
#
# The text is deliberately two clear, separate needs, so `count` proves the extraction split them rather
# than storing one blob.

testData:
  config:
    rawContent: >-
      We need a way to track invoices that are overdue by more than 30 days. Separately, the support team
      needs a single place to see every open ticket for one customer.
    sourceUrl: https://example.com/notes/planning
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    success: "return output.success === true"
    # MORE THAN ZERO, not an exact number: how many needs an LLM finds in a paragraph is not deterministic,
    # so asserting 2 would fail on a reasonable day. Zero is the real failure — it means the text went
    # through and nothing was stored.
    count: "return output.count > 0"
